basic_details.job_title: Jharkhand Agriculture Department Crop Protectors Recruitment 2026 – Apply Offline for 7 Posts
basic_details.short_information: Sahebganj Crop Protectors Recruitment 2026 offers 7 honorarium-based posts of Crop Protectors (Crop Protector) at Plant Protection Centres in Sahebganj district, Jharkhand. The Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative (कृषि, पशुपालन एवं सहकारिता विभाग), Government of Jharkhand, has issued Advertisement No. 01/2026-27 dated 06.11.2026. Applications must go by registered post or speed post to the Office of the District Agriculture Officer, Sahebganj, and must be received by 5 PM on 30 November 2026.

content_sections.heading: About Sahebganj Crop Protectors
content_sections.text: The Crop Protectors posts are part of the Jharkhand Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative's effort to run crop protection and plant protection work effectively at the local level. The selection is conducted by a selection committee chaired by the District Agriculture Officer, Sahebganj, and the selected candidates will work at the Plant Protection Centres in different blocks of Sahebganj district.

content_sections.heading: Where and How to Send
content_sections.text: The application must be sent only by registered post or speed post . Applications received after the last date will not be accepted. The application address is: Office of the District Agriculture Officer, Sanyukt Krishi Bhawan, Sahebganj, PIN Code-816109

content_sections.heading: Posts, Eligibility and Pay
content_sections.text: The 7 Crop Protectors posts are reserved as per the model reservation roster applicable to Sahebganj district. The number of vacancies may change as per administrative need and the decision of the competent authority. The posts are at these Plant Protection Centres: Sahebganj, Borio, Taljhari, Rajmahal, Pathna, Barhait and Barharwa. Minimum Matric/Secondary (10th) pass from a recognised educational institution. At least one training of minimum 5 days under the Directorate of Agriculture and Horticulture, Department of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Cooperative is mandatory. Candidates with longer training will get preference accordingly. Knowledge of the local language. It is a qualifying criterion and carries no merit marks. Proficiency in riding a bicycle and climbing trees. Preference to residents of the block concerned with the Plant Protection Centre. All candidates must submit a valid local resident certificate issued by the competent authority in the prescribed format; candidates claiming reservation must submit a valid caste/category certificate in the prescribed format. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions of the Crop Protectors post. Age is counted as on 30 November 2026, and only the date of birth in the Matric marksheet/certificate is accepted. The minimum age is 18 years. Ex-servicemen get an additional relaxation of five years in the maximum age limit, and must submit the ex-serviceman certificate in time. Monthly honorarium: Rs. 11,851/- only. The engagement is honorarium/remuneration based (मानदेय/पारिश्रमिक आधारित). Tenure: one year or until regular appointment, whichever is earlier. The appointment gives no automatic right to regular appointment, confirmation or service benefits like a regular government employee. The contract may be ended on regular appointment, abolition of the sanctioned post or administrative need.

content_sections.heading: Sahebganj Crop Protectors Job Description
content_sections.text: Crop survey. Spraying of pesticides. Farmer training and awareness. Other work assigned by the office from time to time.

content_sections.heading: Enclosures
content_sections.text: Self-attested photocopies of these documents must be attached to the application: A character/conduct certificate is not needed with the application, but it must be produced at final selection, document verification or joining, as decided by the competent authority.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: All applications will be checked for eligibility and documents. Applications with missing details, without the required certificates, not meeting the essential qualification, or with false or misleading information will be rejected. Valid applications are then evaluated on a total of 100 marks. Training of less than five days is not counted in the merit list, and training days are counted as full days clearly written in the certificate. Where marks are in CGPA/grade, the percentage is worked out by the conversion formula of the board or university concerned. No extra marks are given for a postgraduate or higher qualification, or for more than one degree of the same level. Local language: the declaration in the application is accepted until the provisional merit list. No separate language test is held if the selectable and waiting-list candidates give sufficient proof; otherwise a language test may be held at the discretion of the selection committee/competent authority. Cycling and tree climbing: if the selection committee finds it necessary, a practical test may be taken after the provisional merit list. It carries no merit marks, and a candidate not found capable may be considered ineligible for final selection. A written or oral test may be held at any stage if the selection committee/competent authority finds it necessary. Original certificates of selected/provisionally selected candidates will be verified before final selection, in the format prescribed by the competent authority. When two or more candidates have equal marks, the tie is broken in this order: higher Matric marks/percentage, a valid local language proficiency certificate, higher Intermediate marks/percentage, higher graduation marks/percentage, and higher age. A category-wise merit list will be prepared under the reservation rules, and the final list will be published at the prescribed place. The selection is conducted under the supervision of a selection committee formed by the competent authority.

faq.question: Q1. How many Fasal Rakshak vacancies are there in Sahebganj?
faq.answer: There are 7 Fasal Rakshak posts: 3 for ST, 0 for EWS and 4 Unreserved. The number may change as per administrative need.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date for the Sahebganj Fasal Rakshak application?
faq.answer: The application must be received by 5 PM on 30 November 2026. Applications received after the last date will not be accepted.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is needed for Fasal Rakshak?
faq.answer: Candidates need at least Matric/Secondary (10th) pass and one mandatory training of minimum 5 days under the Directorate of Agriculture and Horticulture, with knowledge of the local language and the ability to ride a bicycle and climb trees.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for Sahebganj Fasal Rakshak?
faq.answer: The minimum age is 18 years as on 30 November 2026; the maximum is 35 years for UR men, 38 years for UR women and 40 years for ST men and women. Ex-servicemen get five extra years.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of a Fasal Rakshak?
faq.answer: The monthly honorarium is Rs. 11,851/- only.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the Fasal Rakshak post?
faq.answer: Fill in the application form printed with the advertisement, attach self-attested certificate copies and send it by registered post or speed post to the Office of the District Agriculture Officer, Sanyukt Krishi Bhawan, Sahebganj, PIN Code-816109.

faq.question: Q7. How will Fasal Rakshak candidates be selected?
faq.answer: Through a 100-mark merit list: up to 70 marks for 10th, 12th and graduation percentages and up to 30 marks for training. A language test, a cycling and tree-climbing test, or a written or oral test may be held if needed.

faq.question: Q8. Is the Fasal Rakshak job permanent?
faq.answer: No. It is an honorarium-based engagement for one year or until regular appointment, whichever is earlier, with no automatic right to regular appointment or confirmation.

faq.question: Q9. Do candidates from the same block get preference?
faq.answer: Yes. Residents of the block concerned with the Plant Protection Centre get preference, and block allocation considers the resident block and the preferences given in the form.

faq.question: Q10. Does extra training give more marks?
faq.answer: Yes. The first 5-day training gives 15 marks, and each additional day beyond five gives 1 mark, up to 15 more marks; training of less than five days is not counted.
